title: Chronic kidney disease: staging, slowing it, and when to refer

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the 2024 KDIGO chronic kidney disease guideline. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: For how long must reduced eGFR or kidney damage persist before chronic kidney disease is diagnosed?
questions.why: Either an eGFR under 60 or a marker of damage such as albuminuria, for more than three months. A single low value after an illness is not chronic kidney disease.

questions.q: Albuminuria category A3 begins at what urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio?
questions.why: A2 is 30 to 300. The albuminuria category predicts progression and cardiovascular risk independently of the eGFR, which is why both are reported.

questions.q: Chronic kidney disease with albuminuria. Which drug class is titrated to the highest tolerated dose?
questions.why: The benefit is on progression, not just blood pressure. A creatinine rise of up to 30% after starting is accepted; a bigger rise prompts a look for renal artery stenosis.

questions.q: Down to what eGFR is an SGLT-2 inhibitor recommended to be started for kidney protection in chronic kidney disease?
questions.why: It is recommended with diabetes, or with an albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 200 or more without diabetes, and can be continued below 20 once started.

questions.q: Which findings are indications for referral to nephrology?
a: A fall in eGFR of more than 5 mL/min a year
questions.why: Refractory hypertension, recurrent potassium problems, and a five-year kidney failure risk over 5% are the others. Referral at eGFR 30 leaves time to plan dialysis access.

questions.q: A patient with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and persistent albuminuria despite an ACE inhibitor and an SGLT-2 inhibitor. Which drug is added?
questions.why: The nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid antagonist reduced kidney and cardiovascular events with less hyperkalemia than spironolactone; potassium must be under 5.0 to start.

questions.q: Below what serum bicarbonate is oral sodium bicarbonate started in chronic kidney disease?
questions.why: Correcting the acidosis slows progression and protects muscle and bone. Fruit and vegetables have a similar alkalising effect.

questions.q: Which imaging contrast is avoided at an eGFR under 30?
questions.why: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. Newer group II gadolinium agents are considered safe at any eGFR. Iodinated contrast is used with hydration when the scan is needed.

questions.q: From what age does a patient with chronic kidney disease qualify for a statin regardless of calculated risk?
questions.why: Chronic kidney disease is a coronary risk equivalent. Under 50, the statin follows the usual risk calculation with kidney disease as a risk enhancer.

questions.q: What daily protein intake is advised for adults with chronic kidney disease not on dialysis?
questions.why: Sodium is kept under 2 g a day. Very low protein diets are not recommended outside specialist supervision because of malnutrition.

questions.q: A creatinine-based eGFR is borderline in a muscular young man. Which test confirms it?
questions.why: Cystatin C is independent of muscle mass. The combined equation is recommended whenever the creatinine-based estimate is likely to be wrong or a decision hangs on it.

questions.q: Which vaccine is specifically recommended for adults with chronic kidney disease who may reach dialysis?
questions.why: Response falls as kidney function falls, so it is given early with antibody checks. Influenza, pneumococcal and COVID-19 vaccines follow the standard schedule.
